quotes.text: Semantic kernel is a free open source kit from Microsoft that connects the software you're already building to an AI model, and then lets the model call your own code back.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The description isn't decoration. If it's vague, the model guesses wrong or skips the function entirely and the whole thing falls apart.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical tip on why plugin descriptions matter.

quotes.text: Function calling is narrower and more repeatable, so you get fewer surprises in production, which is exactly what a business app needs.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why function calling replaced the old planners.

quotes.text: The payoff shows up when a new model arrives. Instead of rewriting your application, you swap the connector and keep everything else.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows the lock-in-free value of connectors.

quotes.text: The model is the part that will change again and again as the technology moves. The wiring between your code and the model is the part you actually control.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable closing thesis about what developers own.

chapters.title: Copilot, Foundry and what comes next

takeaways: Semantic Kernel is open-source middleware that connects your own code to AI models and lets the model call your functions back through plugins.
Function calling replaced the old planners, and vector stores plus retrieval-augmented generation give the model grounded memory of your data.
Microsoft Agent Framework is now the recommended start for new agent projects, but Semantic Kernel stays supported and its concepts carry straight over.
hook: Semantic Kernel sits under Microsoft's AI tools, yet almost nobody explains what it actually does. This episode breaks it down for developers and curious IT pros: the kernel, plugins, function calling, memory, connectors and how it relates to Copilot and the Microsoft Agent Framework. You will know when to reach for it and which ideas carry over to any AI stack.
